term: Course of Action Display and Evaluation Tool
definition: Course of Action Display and Evaluation Tool (CADET) was a research program, and the eponymous prototype software system, that applied knowledge-based techniques of Artificial Intelligence to the problem of battle planning.
details: CADET was also known as Course of Action Display and Elaboration Tool. It was considered an early example of such systems and was funded by the United States Army and by the Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA). CADET influenced a later DARPA program called RAID which in turn produced a technology adopted by the United States Army and the United States Marine Corps.

explainer.lead: CADET was an early research prototype that used knowledge-based artificial intelligence to help display and evaluate possible battle plans. Its importance is historical: it influenced later DARPA work whose technology was adopted by the United States Army and Marine Corps.

tiers.eli5: Imagine planning a complicated game with several possible moves. CADET was an experimental computer helper that showed possible battle plans and helped people judge them. It was an early attempt to use computer knowledge to support planning.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers should understand CADET as a historical research prototype, not a documented modern software package. Its pattern is knowledge-based decision support for displaying and evaluating alternative battle plans; its implementation language, interfaces, evaluation metrics, and deployment tooling are unspecified.
tiers.paperLevel: CADET denotes both a research program and its eponymous prototype applying knowledge-based AI to course-of-action display and evaluation in battle planning. No formal model, algorithm, dataset, or quantitative results are specified; its documented lineage is CADET → RAID → technology adopted by the United States Army and United States Marine Corps.

explainer.example: A planner could compare one proposed attack plan with an alternative route: CADET’s role would be to display both courses of action and support their evaluation. This illustrates its purpose without assuming a particular interface or scoring method.

explainer.intuition: Battle planning involves choosing among possible courses of action. CADET’s idea was to use stored knowledge to make those alternatives visible and support their evaluation.
howItWorks: Frame battle planning as a choice among courses of action.
Apply knowledge-based AI techniques to the planning problem.
Display candidate courses of action for inspection.
Support evaluation so alternatives can be compared.
explainer.whyItMatters: CADET was an early example of knowledge-based AI for battle planning. It influenced DARPA’s RAID program, which produced technology later adopted by the United States Army and United States Marine Corps.
misconceptions: CADET was not RAID; it was an earlier program that influenced RAID.
Its name also had the alternate expansion Course of Action Display and Elaboration Tool.
It was a research program and prototype, not a documented operational deployment.
